A1.justification: Both PDFs describe EgoTextVQA and contain the complete main paper and Appendices A–D. Text, figures, tables and experimental descriptions are readable and can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original model evaluations, heuristic experiments, human studies and evaluator-agreement results in Sections 4–5 and Appendices B–C.

after.justification: v2 retains the original model evaluations, heuristic experiments, human studies and evaluator-agreement results.

M1.justification: The dataset-construction pipeline and investigated procedures remain unchanged, including timestamp-aware sampling, scene-text super-resolution and auxiliary OCR inputs. No new algorithm or model component is introduced.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same outdoor-driving and indoor-housekeeping coverage, question categories and real-time QA scenarios. The corrected Shopping question count does not introduce new coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged throughout the experiments. Tables 3–4 explicitly rename the InternVL2 rows as InternVL2-8B and InternVL2-26B; these variants were already identifiable from v1's backbone specifications and Table 8.

E3.justification: Table 1 revises the reported Shopping subset size from 258 to 358 questions, retaining 78 videos. This corrects a previously stated sample count; it does not establish that evaluations were rerun. Sampling procedures, resolutions, metrics and human-study settings otherwise remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The frame-selection, temporal-sampling, resolution, OCR-input and combined-heuristic analyses are retained, alongside the supplementary human studies and qualitative cases in Appendices B–C.

E5.justification: Both retain the two human-study rounds and Appendix C's Pearson correlations of 0.80 and 0.87 and accuracy agreement kappa of 0.77. No new repeated-run information, uncertainty estimates or statistical tests appear.

E6.justification: Table 1 changes Shopping from 258 to 358 questions, making the indoor category counts sum to the stated 2,216. Model scores and plotted findings remain unchanged, including Gemini 1.5 Pro's 33.4% outdoor and 34.4% indoor accuracy in Tables 3–4.

T1.justification: Neither version presents formal theoretical results or proofs. No substantive mathematical definitions, assumptions or derivations are added or revised.

C1.justification: Section 3.2 drops v1's assertion that EgoTextVQA is the first VideoQA dataset to introduce real-time QA, stating only that it introduces real-time QA. The main benchmark, model-performance and heuristic contributions are retained.

C2.justification: The explanations involving OCR difficulty, temporal grounding, external knowledge and model failures remain substantively unchanged. The limitation concerning insufficient ground-truth answer diversity and proposed answer enrichment is also retained.

D1.justification: The filtering and annotation procedures, model prompts, OCR processing details, evaluator version and dataset-access link are retained. Appendix B.1's more explicit InternVL2 naming repeats model-size information already available in v1.

R1.justification: v2 adds nine references, including Invariant Grounding for Video Question Answering and Scene-Text Grounding for Text-Based Video Question Answering, and removes HourVideo. These are limited background-citation updates; the related-work narrative remains largely intact, with the real-time novelty assertion narrowed.

P1.justification: Several paragraphs in the dataset description, results discussion and conclusion are condensed and copyedited. v2 also adds an acknowledgements section, renumbers affiliations and clarifies model terminology while preserving the main narrative and appendix organization.

P2.justification: All nine figures and seventeen tables are retained. Changes include explicit model-size labels in Tables 3–4, modest spacing and page-flow adjustments, and removal of printed page numbers; the visualizations are not substantively redesigned.

improvement.justification: v2 resolves Table 1's internal count inconsistency, narrows the real-time novelty assertion and improves some prose and model labels. These provide modest gains in accuracy and clarity. The experimental evidence and substantive limitations remain unchanged.
